title: Structure Of Semisimple Lie Algebras
notes: Open by naming the chapter as a passage from representation-theoretic triangularization to the rigid combinatorics of roots. The lecture will keep one concrete model in view, sl(3), then use sl(2,R) to show how real forms and Cartan decompositions change the geometry.

title: Chapter Route
notes: Use this roadmap to prevent the chapter from feeling like a list of unrelated structure theorems. The first block makes solvable and nilpotent behavior visible; the middle block extracts roots from a Cartan subalgebra; the last block compares complex and real forms.

title: Lie And Engel As Termination Tests
notes: Present Lie and Engel theorems through finite diagnostics rather than full proofs. Lie theorem pushes solvable representations toward upper triangular form, while Engel theorem identifies nilpotence by forcing repeated commutators to terminate. The chain dimensions give students a concrete clock.

title: Two Chains, Two Kinds Of Collapse
notes: The derived chain measures how quickly commutators erase nonabelian behavior, while the central descending chain measures how far brackets can move before all motion vanishes. The triangular five-by-five model is deliberately small, but the qualitative distinction survives in arbitrary finite-dimensional settings.

title: Cartan Subalgebras Are Regularizers
notes: Move from nilpotent collapse to regular semisimple measurement. A Cartan subalgebra is not chosen merely for convenience; it is the probe whose adjoint eigenvalues split the algebra. In sl(3), regular diagonal elements have the expected two-dimensional centralizer, while singular ones gain extra symmetries.

title: Root Space Decomposition
notes: This is the algebraic hinge of the chapter. Once a Cartan subalgebra h is fixed, every nonzero root alpha records a simultaneous eigenspace for ad h. The decomposition separates the silent Cartan directions from root directions that carry the bracket geometry.

title: The A2 Root Picture In sl(3)
notes: Use the hexagon as a memory device for the six off-diagonal matrix directions in sl(3). The two simple roots generate the positive cone, and the remaining roots are forced by sign reversal and addition. The picture is combinatorial, but it encodes bracket information.

title: Root Strings And Reflections
notes: Root strings explain why root systems are not arbitrary point clouds. Moving along a root direction stops at integral endpoints, and reflection across the perpendicular hyperplane preserves the whole set. This is where Cartan integers begin controlling the geometry of the diagram.

title: Brackets Follow Root Addition
notes: The bracket rule is the operational reason roots matter. If X_alpha and X_beta are root vectors, their bracket has weight alpha plus beta when that sum is a root, lands in h when beta is minus alpha, and otherwise vanishes. The sl(3) table verifies the rule explicitly.

title: From Root Pattern To Algebra
notes: Emphasize the structural payoff: after the Cartan subalgebra and roots are known, much of the semisimple algebra is constrained by a finite diagram and integer structure constants. This does not remove analysis or proof, but it turns a large algebra into inspected local interactions.

title: Real Forms Change The Metric Signature
notes: The complex root diagram stays a guide, but a real form changes which directions are compact, split, or mixed. The Killing form becomes a diagnostic: compact directions tend to negative sign, while split directions contribute positive sign in the sl(2,R) model.

title: Cartan Decomposition In sl(2,R)
notes: Use this slide to separate the involution from the bracket bookkeeping. The Cartan involution theta fixes k and negates p; the bracket relations then say k is a subalgebra, k acts on p, and p brackets back into k. This is the infinitesimal seed of symmetric spaces.

title: Classical Families As Root Machines
notes: The classical series are best introduced as recipes for roots rather than as isolated matrix names. A_n uses differences of coordinate weights, B_n and C_n add short or long coordinate roots, and D_n keeps only paired sign combinations. Counts become a first consistency check.

title: Notebook Diagnostics As Evidence
notes: Connect the lecture deck back to the companion notebook. Each computation is a witness for one structural claim: chain termination, regular centralizer dimension, A2 root closure, reflection preservation, bracket addition, Cartan sign splitting, and classical root counts. The goal is reproducible intuition.

title: Applied Lab
notes: Invite students to perturb the finite models instead of passively accepting the diagrams. Change the diagonal element in sl(3), choose a different pair of simple roots, or swap the Cartan involution in sl(2,R). The checks reveal which statements are robust and which require regularity.

title: Recap
notes: Close by tracing one continuous story. Solvable and nilpotent pieces can be triangularized or made to collapse; Cartan subalgebras expose roots; roots dictate bracket interactions; real forms and Cartan decompositions turn the complex structure into geometry. This prepares the later symmetric-space chapters.
